facts.text: Gallium Arsenide Solar Arrays was deployed at Asteroid 433 Eros (South Pole) during NEAR Shoemaker at Eros in 1996.
facts.source: JHU APL Technical Digest / Jenkins et al.

facts.text: Four rigid solar array wings spanning 5.6 meters total, utilizing high-efficiency GaAs cells generating 1,800 watts at 1 AU from the Sun.
facts.source: JHU APL Technical Digest / Jenkins et al.

facts.text: Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the lunar environment.
Demonstrated that gallium arsenide photovoltaic cells could survive severe deep-space radiation belts and micrometeroid bombardment without catastrophic voltage loss.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Asteroid 433 Eros (South Pole).
A permanent human and robotic monument celebrating space exploration on the Moon.

scenes.kids: I am Gallium Arsenide Solar Arrays. I arrived here at Asteroid 433 Eros (South Pole) in 1996.
scenes.explorer: Gallium Arsenide Solar Arrays, NEAR Shoemaker at Eros: deployed at Asteroid 433 Eros (South Pole) in 1996.

scenes.kids: Take a look at how I was built. Every part of me had a special purpose.
scenes.explorer: Four rigid solar array wings spanning 5.6 meters total, utilizing high-efficiency GaAs cells generating 1,800 watts at 1 AU from the Sun.

scenes.kids: Out here, there is no air or weather like on Earth, so I had to work smoothly in the cold.
scenes.explorer: Designed to withstand radiation, cosmic dust, and extreme temperature swings without failing.

scenes.kids: Demonstrated that gallium arsenide photovoltaic cells could survive severe deep-space radiation belts and micrometeroid bombardment without catastrophic voltage loss.
scenes.explorer: Demonstrated that gallium arsenide photovoltaic cells could survive severe deep-space radiation belts and micrometeroid bombardment without catastrophic voltage loss.

scenes.kids: My mission finished, but I stay here resting peacefully on the surface.
scenes.explorer: Fate: left on surface. Position recorded at coordinates [4.2, -3.5].

scenes.kids: Everything I learned showed humanity how to explore deeper into space.
scenes.explorer: A milestone in planetary science and permanent historical artifact.
